tasks.short: Encourage exploration and perseverance to prepare students for later grades

steps.what: Encourage students to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks

tasks.design: Retain direct encouragement and exploration with the teacher. Existing learning resources in {LMS} may supply opportunities, but no generated motivational message replaces the interaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Encouragement must respond to the student's actual difficulty and interests.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital resources can offer options without knowing which response will help this student.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a useful challenge from a task that needs a different approach.
tasks.human_edge: Notice effort, offer credible encouragement and preserve the student's agency.
tasks.altitude: Teacher contact and encouragement remain unchanged.

reach.task: Support a student through a difficult learning attempt
reach.learn: Specific feedback, scaffolding and avoiding empty praise

evidence.claim: Context-sensitive encouragement and perseverance support are relational teaching work.

assumptions: Boundary covers the teacher's direct encouragement, not building a resource catalogue or writing a progress report.
The teacher elicits interests and observes the response during s1, retaining all time. No structured motivation score or inferred emotion is assumed; uncertain needs require direct conversation.
Review native learning-resource access before future additions; no new software or data collection is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the interaction and tools are unchanged. Support overlapping tutoring is counted once.
unknowns: Current opportunities and barriers to student participation
research_questions: Which teacher responses help a student choose a constructive next attempt?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine encouragement and persistent difficulty retain teacher contact; no motivation-score or message-generation saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Use audiovisual equipment and materials to supplement presentations

steps.what: Select suitable audiovisual aids and check their accuracy, access and lesson relevance
Assemble selected media and equipment settings for the supplementary presentation
Use computers, audiovisual aids and other equipment to supplement classroom presentations

tasks.design: Use native reusable layouts and saved media sequences in {DOCS} with the {OTHER} presentation software. The teacher selects and checks assets, tests the prepared package and operates equipment while responding to the class.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated media assembly and settings can consume preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native presentation layouts and saved settings can reuse the teacher's exact selections.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a useful explanation and responding when an aid confuses rather than helps.
tasks.human_edge: Connect what students see or hear to the concept and adapt the live explanation.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated assembly; content choices and classroom presentation remain human.

reach.task: Review an accessible media presentation format
reach.learn: Accessibility, media rights and pedagogical relevance

evidence.claim: Reusable presentation layouts can reduce media assembly without selecting content or delivering the lesson.

assumptions: Boundary covers media selection, package assembly and classroom use, not a separate lesson-content authoring task.

The teacher produces approved asset identifier or file, exact clip bounds, sequence, accompanying text and accessibility needs in s1, with selection and capture fully counted. In retained s2 time the teacher applies saved settings, checks links, playback and output; no free structured media manifest is assumed.
Missing rights, captions, files or reliable playback trigger manual substitution and existing backup materials. No model invents images or rewrites lesson meaning.
Test native reusable layouts and presentation settings first. If assembly is already automated, the lower scenario applies; equipment runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Existing templates, equipment reliability and actual assembly share
research_questions: Does native reuse reduce assembly time after checking accessibility and actual classroom playback?

already_counted.description: Asset selection and live classroom use remain.
Package setup, playback checks and manual fallback remain.

incremental.description: Teacher refreshes asset links, layouts and saved equipment settings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 less two upkeep hours gives net=8. High assumes assembly halves through native reuse; low assumes existing reuse and playback exceptions leave only upkeep-equivalent gain. Selection and delivery retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate on development, evaluation and revision of middle school programs

steps.what: Review middle school program evidence and identify issues for collaborative evaluation
Collaborate with teachers and administrators to evaluate programs and agree proposed revisions
Document and verify proposed program development and revisions for the programme owner

loop.purpose: Express agreed changes in a coherent programme proposal
loop.input: Exact current programme passages, agreed revisions, conditions and unresolved questions
loop.output: Tracked draft revisions with brief references and an unresolved list
loop.check: Teacher checks every change against the agreement, curriculum intent, sequencing, resources and retained conditions; new commitments or silently resolved questions are rejected
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then manual revision for unresolved text
loop.why_not_simpler: Native tracked changes handle versioning first; reconciling agreed prose edits still requires language judgement

tasks.design: Keep programme evaluation and agreement with teachers and administrators. Use {DOCS} tracked revisions and a bounded drafting loop for agreed wording; the teacher verifies the exact proposal before handing it to the programme owner for formal decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Translating a shared agreement into consistent programme wording can require repeated editing.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-constrained drafting can support wording after people agree the changes.
tasks.still_hard: Judging educational value and reaching agreement under staffing or timetable constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge a weak proposal and explain practical classroom consequences.
tasks.altitude: Less revision composition; programme judgement and formal adoption rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a traceable programme change proposal
reach.learn: Curriculum progression, consultation and change governance

evidence.claim: A bounded drafting tool can express agreed document changes, but it does not evaluate programme quality or create stakeholder agreement.

assumptions: Boundary ends at the teacher's verified proposal; programme-owner adoption and colleagues' participation remain outside and unchanged.

The teacher produces findings in s1 and captures exact agreed changes, responsible owners, constraints and unresolved questions in s2. All review, discussion and capture time is retained; incomplete agreement returns to direct discussion or manual wording.
Test native tracked changes and reusable programme structures before model use. No pupil-level records or generated pupil evaluation are needed.
The retained 15 share hours in s3 include checking all proposed changes, correcting wording and final proposal release. Changes after review void that release.
Overlap with lesson planning or curriculum work is allocated once.
unknowns: Actual revision-writing share and programme approval route
research_questions: Does drafting assistance preserve every agreed condition after full teacher review?

already_counted.description: Programme review, collaborative judgement and agreement capture remain.
Revision checking, corrections and proposal release remain.

incremental.description: Teacher audits revision fidelity and refreshes document controls after updates.

approvals.approved_version: Exact programme proposal with tracked changes, agreement brief and unresolved questions checked before handover; any edit requires renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 less three upkeep hours gives net=7. High assumes wording effort falls 40 percent; low assumes disputed or complex clauses leave only upkeep-equivalent gain. Review and collaboration retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Guide students with adjustment or academic problems or special interests

steps.what: Listen to students' adjustment concerns, academic difficulties or special interests
Guide and counsel students and agree support or exploration next steps

tasks.design: Retain student guidance and counselling with the teacher within existing support boundaries. Approved support information in {DOCS} may help explain options; the interaction and referral judgement remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: The student's concern can be sensitive, incomplete or different from the initial description.
tasks.enabler_now: Information access does not remove the need to listen and clarify.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing when a concern requires specialist support rather than classroom advice.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, respect preferences and recognise the limits of the teacher's role.
tasks.altitude: Guidance and referral authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify a student's support question for specialist advice
reach.learn: Referral boundaries and factual, respectful communication

evidence.claim: Student guidance depends on contextual conversation and recognising when specialist help is needed.

assumptions: Boundary covers direct guidance, not diagnosis, formal placement, or a separate support report. Specialist work outside the teacher's remit is unchanged.

The teacher elicits needs and preferences in s1 and s2, with all contact time retained. No structured problem category, emotional inference or free pupil profile is assumed; uncertainty requires clarification.
Review native support-information access first; no new tool, recording or pupil scoring is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because the conversation and process remain unchanged. Guidance shared with another support task is allocated once.
unknowns: Local guidance limits and available specialist support
research_questions: Which student concerns most often need referral beyond classroom guidance?

already_counted.description: Listening, guidance and referral discussion remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine interest guidance and sensitive adjustment concerns retain the human interaction and judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Media assembly and agreed programme wording can receive limited support; encouragement, guidance and educational judgement retain their full human time.
reach: Review media accessibility and programme changes with instructional coordinators
Clarify specialist support questions with special education teachers
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with reusable presentation materials and clearer programme proposals who remains present for students' challenges and choices.

job.title: Middle School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
